name: Sir William Jones
credit: Sir William Jones, by Sir Joshua Reynolds, 1767 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Sir William Jones (1746–1794) was a British orientalist and judge in Calcutta, founder of the Asiatic Society (1784), who first proposed the kinship of Sanskrit with Greek, Latin and the other Indo-European languages. He wrote English verse as well as translations from Persian and Sanskrit.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: To an Infant Newly Born
poems.author: Sir William Jones
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
On parent's knees, a naked new-born child,
Weeping thou sat'st while all around thee smiled;
So live, that sinking in thy long last sleep.
Calm thou may'st smile, while all around thee weep.
